blueprint_tool_entry: this repository's own ceremony loop (state/loop-workflow.js, kb/ceremonies/, state/lessons.jsonl) as the instance that runs today. docs/architecture/blueprint.json carries no tool_entries row for it and no impact_map row for this composition - its own open question asks whether compose-operators and compose-improvement-loop are deliberately stateless - so the nearest impact row is 'the durable executor is replaced', which names compose-loop
standard: none adopted; the loop shape (one iteration moves the metric furthest from its target, gated by an evaluation that can say no, checkpointed each fire) is this repository's design, TARGET T9.1 (T-t9-01) and the compose-improvement-loop skill. JSON Schema 2020-12 governs the loop declaration check and RFC 9457 the failure body; both are reached through shapes harness/evaluation already ships

differs_in_execution_model: execution_model: one process holds the whole loop vs no process between iterations
checkpoint_store: in-memory vs a file per checkpoint
survives_process_loss: a fresh binding refuses vs a fresh binding resumes

live.component: this repository's ceremony loop: state/loop-workflow.js fires research, authoring, a ceremony review and an improve pass per section; its records are kb/ceremonies/ceremony-NN-review.json and -improve.json, state/lessons.jsonl and state/loop.json

design_notes: The gate is not declared here. harness/evaluation/interface.py is imported under its own module name and its adapter is loaded by path; every candidate is decided by that capability's evaluate call, and this harness re-states no case set, rubric, verdict or baseline logic. test.sh section 6 asserts the identity of those objects rather than trusting the claim.

Extensions to the owner skills' shapes, so a reader can tell them from the skills: compose-improvement-loop's CandidateOutcome (promoted|declined) is carried here as the decision field of an IterationRecord that also names the metric, the distance before and after, the checkpoint in force and whether it advanced - the scorecard half TARGET T9.1 fixes and that skill does not shape. compose-loop's terminated_by and termination_class are used verbatim, three members and no fourth.

compose-improvement-loop's promote_revision writes to a capability registry; there is no registry running here, so promotion in this harness moves a checkpoint and a metric value and writes no target file at all. no_in_place_edit_operation() asserts the interface has nowhere to name one. Wiring promotion to a registry is named as the open gap, not simulated.

The escalation for a capped loop returns the registered urn:agentic:problem:deadline-exceeded and names the proposed urn:agentic:problem:iteration-ceiling-reached in detail, which is compose-loop's own open-question default; no unregistered type is minted.

The scorecard fixture's metric ids are TARGET T9's row names (measured_done_share, proposed_share, stale_status_rows) and its numbers are fixture values chosen to exercise a failed, an inconclusive and four passing gates. Nothing in this harness measures this repository's actual scorecard.
Running out of candidates for a metric is a typed refusal (criterion-unresolvable), never a fourth termination reason.

Conformance against dryrun exits 0 at 25/25: scorecard digest sha256:e94b0b2ac2ff374450b8befb18bd78ae over 3 metrics and 6 candidates; 6 iterations working measured_done_share, measured_done_share, stale_status_rows, stale_status_rows, proposed_share, measured_done_share - the furthest metric each time, never the first listed; gate outcomes failed, passed, inconclusive, passed, passed, passed; 4 promoted and 2 declined; both declined iterations left the standing checkpoint (ck-a16c7afd5613 and ck-9629dc65a393) in place with checkpoint_advanced false; terminated_by verdict_pass (stop) with 3/3 targets held at 1500000 of 3000000 micros; the same scorecard under a ceiling of 2 terminated_by iteration_ceiling (cap) escalating urn:agentic:problem:deadline-exceeded carrying the proposed iteration-ceiling-reached suffix; under a 600000-micro budget, budget_ceiling (cap) at 500000; a loop declared with no iteration ceiling refused with urn:agentic:problem:document-invalid (422) leaving no checkpoint; a re-delivered iteration returned the identical record and wrote no new checkpoint. The minimal call is 22 lines of caller code, under 40, naming no driver storage.
measured.swap: conformance before with dryrun and after with second, selected by ADAPTER= with no code edit (the sha256 of interface.py, call.py and conformance.py is identical before and after: d3ab54d66fa12f8623ff227515e8624a84a5b7aeccc20b37ab893d97d1d5e7be); both exit 0 at 25/25 and the merged report shows adapters_run 2, record_divergence 0, selected_by configuration. Both drivers wrote byte-identical iteration records, records_digest sha256:03731dea2b4a582f164b39774dde4535 on each side. The pair differs on all three declared axes: bounded-in-process vs one-iteration-per-fire, in-memory vs file checkpoints, and a fresh binding refusing with typed problem details vs resuming from the checkpoint - so it is not one driver run twice. call.py prints identical tables and identical PROOF lines on both.
measured.breakage: conformance --break-gate replaces the promotion rule with one that advances the checkpoint whatever the gate said, changing nothing else. Both drivers exit 1 identically on the same two checks - C5 (a failed gate declines and holds the checkpoint) reading 'cand-md-01: promoted, checkpoint ck-a16c7afd5613->ck-b63bcad4c534' and C6 (an inconclusive gate is treated exactly like a failed one) reading 'cand-sr-01: promoted/None' - while the unbounded refusal stays document-invalid and the capped loop still terminates by iteration_ceiling, which locates the fault in the checkpoint rule rather than in the declaration check, the ceiling or either driver. This is the gate that cannot say no, reproduced on purpose.
